items.ftc-ai-consumer-protection::section-5-de: The FTC Act prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce. Applied to AI, a representation, omission or practice about an AI system's capabilities, outputs or aims is deceptive — and enforceable by the Commission — if it is likely to mislead a consumer acting reasonably in the circumstances, to the consumer's detriment. Claims that a system is accurate, helpful, reliable or truthful, and the implicit claims created by how a product is marketed, are all held to that standard.
items.ftc-ai-consumer-protection::undisclosed-: The Commission's July 2026 proposed policy statement addresses suppressing or steering the accuracy of AI outputs: where consumers reasonably expect a system to pursue their stated objectives faithfully, altering or steering its outputs toward undisclosed objectives — for any reason, including in an effort to comply with state-law mandates — can itself deceive consumers in violation of section 5. Truthful, non-misleading disclosure that the system prioritises objectives other than those users requested or would expect can avert deception; silence cannot.
items.ftc-ai-consumer-protection::claim-substa: Deception authority requires an entity to substantiate the representations it makes about its products or services with sufficient evidence before disseminating them. For AI systems this covers claims of accuracy, capability and benchmark performance: an unsubstantiated claim that a model can reliably perform a task is actionable whether or not anyone is actually deceived.
items.ftc-ai-consumer-protection::enforcement-: The Commission enforces section 5 against AI-related misconduct through administrative consent orders and federal court actions, including against deceptive claims about what an AI product can do (legal-replacement chatbots, AI content detectors, facial-recognition and screening tools are among past matters). Remedies include cease-and-desist obligations, mandated disclosures and, for violations of orders or the rule on misleading claims, civil penalties.
